chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the man who is in need of his son's wealth. He said: 'He may eat from it whatever he wishes, without extravagance.'

And he said: 'In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): The son does not take anything from his father's wealth except by his permission, and the father takes from his son's wealth whatever he wishes, and it is permissible for him to have relations with his son's slave girl if the son has not already had relations with her.'
And he mentioned that the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said to a man: 'You and your wealth are for your father.'
ai.seo_question: What are the financial rights of a father regarding his son's wealth in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi establishes the asymmetrical financial authority in Shia jurisprudence, where the father holds unilateral rights over his son's wealth without requiring permission, provided he avoids extravagance (israf). The narration links this legal principle to the Prophetic tradition 'You and your wealth belong to your father,' while also extending the father's right to include utilizing the son's female slave, reflecting the socio-economic context of the time. This ruling underscores the patriarchal structure of family finance, distinguishing the father's inherent right from the son's dependent status.
